source.title: From Input to Output: A Flexible Agent for Dual-End Interpretation of Sparse Autoencoder Features
source.authors: De-Wen Liu; Zi-Xu Li; Jonathan Pan; Zhao-Yu Wu; Zi-Jun Yao; Juan-Zi Li; Xiao-Zhi Wang

page_placements.theme: Residual polysemanticity and context-dependent feature explanations

record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE features as the objects of its interpretation method, but does not test superposition, representational geometry, or the claim versions about SAE features as canonical units.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates the quality and cost of SAE-feature interpretations, not whether sparse features are stored as overlapping directions or whether SAEs recover complete, stable units. DAFI-versus-baseline scores, probing costs, and steering-filter results do not test the claim versions. The endpoint-relation distribution is recorded as a related finding under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study builds and scores an agent that interprets GemmaScope and Qwen-Scope SAE features. It uses SAE features as given objects. Its results are interpretation scores, token costs, skill transfer, judge and human agreement, and steering-filter gains. None of these bears on toy-model geometry, the capacity account of polysemanticity, whether LLM features are spread across neurons or recovered by SAEs, whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units, or feature dimensionality. The Equivalent/Shift/Break analysis concerns the semantic correspondence between a feature's activating inputs and its intervention outputs. That is a related but different construct, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that input and output endpoints often differ, which motivates explicit functional interpretation. They also conclude that DAFI improves Input and Output scores over SAGE and Token Change, that short-context probing cuts inference volume, and that skills transfer across LLM–SAE settings. They draw no conclusion about superposition or the canonicality of SAE features.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops an agent for SAE-feature interpretation; it does not reproduce the toy-model method or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: not stated for the claim; interpretation scores vary by layer, but those results do not test the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: The sample is 215 GemmaScope Gemma-2-2B features whose input and output interpretations both passed. Of these, 63.7% were classified Shift, 7.0% Break and 29.3% Equivalent, so 70.7% have non-equivalent input and output semantics. Classification was LLM-assisted with author review; inter-annotator relation-label kappa was 0.576.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features often promote output semantics distinct from the semantics that activate them, so single-endpoint labels misdescribe them.

record.problems: The semantic-relation analysis is restricted to 215 features whose endpoint interpretations passed; the classification uses LLM assistance with author review, and no uncertainty estimates are stated. These results do not measure representational geometry or validate SAE-feature completeness, stability, or canonicality.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included because they measure interpretation scores, agent efficiency, human/judge agreement, or steering selection rather than any claim version.

untested.parts: Toy-model superposition, the sparsity-dependent transition and regular geometry; no toy models are trained.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or gives important features dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure; neurons are not analysed.
Whether LLM features are distributed across neurons or recoverable by SAEs. Interpretability pass rates reflect the agent's quality on pretrained SAEs, not a test of recovery.
Completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, and canonicality of SAE features; not examined.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional; not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T4 and uses_without_test calls are confirmed. Row r1 is correctly unlinked. The 215 features are a selected subset of a 250-feature pool (those with both endpoints passing), which limits generality. Human relation-label agreement was only moderate (70%, kappa 0.576). The remaining results (baseline tables, probing volume, threshold robustness, AxBench filtering) are method-performance results and are rightly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Whether LLM features are spread across neurons or whether SAE dictionaries recover sparse features as claimed.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B (GemmaScope gemmascope-res-16k residual-stream SAEs)
rows.operation_detail: Classified input/output semantic relations for features whose input- and output-side interpretations both passed.
rows.measure: Classification of the semantic relation between activating-input and intervention-output interpretations
rows.locator: Section 4.4, Figure 4; relation definitions in Table 4
rows.note: Relations were classified with LLM assistance and author review. This reports semantic correspondence between interpretation endpoints, not representation geometry or SAE-feature completeness, stability, or canonicality.

relation.reason: Treats SAE features as supplied analysis objects and measures interpretation quality, efficiency, semantic correspondence and steering-feature selection.

tranche.reason: Uses pretrained SAE features to develop and evaluate an interpretation agent; its endpoint-relation analysis does not test any listed superposition claim version.

source_check.notes: The 70.7% applies only to the 215 features whose endpoint interpretations both passed, not the full feature population. Semantic endpoint differences do not establish representation geometry or SAE-feature completeness, stability or canonicality.
